summary: 80-foot forest lookout reported completed in September 1930 on the Mossy Head-Niceville road; the page says it went to the War Department in 1940.

facts.agency: Choctawhatchee National Forest, then the War Department

events.note: Announced as completed in a September 1930 Pensacola News Journal report, quoted on the source page. The tower was 80 feet tall.
The source says the lookout facilities were transferred to the War Department.

evidence.supports: completion of a new 80-foot lookout tower at Ramer creek in 1930
evidence.quote: Forestry officials yesterday announced completion of a new 80-foot lookout tower at Ramer creek on the Mossy Head-Niceville road.

evidence.supports: the report is attributed to the Pensacola News Journal
visitors were welcome to go up the tower, per the 1930 report
evidence.quote: Visitors are welcome to ascend the tower for a view of the forest, they said.

evidence.supports: the page places the tower in Okaloosa County
the page lists the Choctawhatchee National Forest, then the War Department
lookout facilities transferred to the War Department in 1940
evidence.quote: 1940: The lookout facilities were transferred to the War Department.

evidence.supports: Mossy Head is an unincorporated community in Walton County
evidence.quote: Mossy Head is an unincorporated community in Walton County, Florida

notes_for_editor: Only one source: a page on easternuslookouts.weebly.com that quotes a September 1930 Pensacola News Journal report and a 1940 transfer note. The newspaper and any government record were not read directly. The page says Okaloosa County, but Mossy Head, which the road name includes, is in Walton County, so the county is unconfirmed; the record coordinates were not checked against a map. The record agency string matches the page. No staffing, fire or current-condition source was found in two web searches. A search snippet suggested Congress moved the national forest to the War Department on 27 June 1940; it was not read and is not used.
